claims.text: Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping concluded a three-day state visit in Washington on Friday without reaching an agreement to pause their countries' artificial intelligence arms race.
At a White House state dinner on Thursday, Bernie Sanders noted the net worths of attending tech leaders: Elon Musk ($928bn), Jensen Huang ($186bn), Lisa Su ($3.5bn), and Tim Cook ($3.1bn).

Representative Ro Khanna stated that Donald Trump could have looked like a statesman by establishing technical working groups with companies like DeepSeek, Moonshot, Alibaba, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Gemini to commit to a pause on self-improving AI.
China aims for next-generation smart terminals and AI agents to achieve over 90% penetration by 2030.

At the National Archives, Donald Trump told reporters regarding founding documents: 'Ours goes 250 years, which is great, and we're proud of. Theirs goes 6,000 years. So there's a little difference between 6,000 and 250.'
Donald Trump mocked former President Joe Biden's use of an autopen while showing Xi Jinping presidential portraits in the White House colonnade.
Joe Biden is represented by an autopen instead of a traditional portrait in the White House Presidential Walk of Fame.
Former White House aide Sarah Matthews criticized Trump's autopen joke, stating: 'Nothing says "America First" like mocking a former American president in front of a communist dictator.'
Donald Trump personally welcomed Xi Jinping at Joint Base Andrews, an honor that had not been extended to a foreign leader at the base since 1962.
The United States and China agreed to extend a trade truce by two months to allow U.S. access to Chinese rare earth elements and Chinese access to select advanced American semiconductor chips.
Donald Trump announced plans to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China in November, while Xi Jinping plans to attend the G20 Leaders' Summit in Miami in December.
Prior to the conclusion of Thursday's meeting, China's state news agency called on the United States to oppose formal independence for Taiwan.
U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated on Wednesday that a trade truce due to expire in November would be extended until January.
The current trade truce builds on the 'Busan deal' agreed upon by Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in South Korea in October 2025.
Al Jazeera published a report detailing which countries walked out of Benjamin Netanyahu's address to the UN General Assembly.
More than 100 people were arrested during protests against Benjamin Netanyahu's UN speech in New York, including Susan Sarandon, Chelsea Manning, and Caleb Hearon.
Dozens of UN delegates walked out of the General Assembly hall as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu took the stage.
In response to delegates walking out of his speech, Benjamin Netanyahu said: 'If there are any other moral cowards who haven't left the hall, please do so now.'
Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas delivered a recorded video address to the UN General Assembly after being denied a U.S. entry visa.
According to UN figures, 23 Palestinians have been killed in settler attacks in 2026, and 72 since the beginning of 2023.
Benjamin Netanyahu labeled Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan a 'tyrant' and accused him of supporting Hamas.
Benjamin Netanyahu called allegations of Israeli genocide in Gaza 'the biggest lie of the century' during his UN General Assembly address.
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani responded to Benjamin Netanyahu's speech by accusing him of using the UN podium to repeat 'baseless lies meant to sanitize his genocide against Palestinians.'
The United States and Israel jointly launched air strikes against Tehran in February.
Benjamin Netanyahu cited retired U.S. Colonel John Spencer as stating that Israel 'has done more to prevent civilian casualties in war than any other military in history.'
Israeli military strikes in Gaza have killed more than 73,900 people since October 2023.
In September 2025, the United Nations Independent International Commission of Inquiry reported that Israel committed genocide against Palestinians in Gaza.
The UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry reported in June that Israeli forces killed over 20,000 children and injured 44,000 in Gaza since October 2023.
Iran announced it has presented the United States with a seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
Oil prices fell by over two percent on Friday following optimism surrounding a potential U.S.-Iran diplomatic deal.
The benchmark U.S. 10-year Treasury yield reached its highest level since 2007 on Thursday amid inflation concerns over the Strait of Hormuz closure.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi proposed reopening the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the U.S. lifts its naval blockade, waives oil sanctions, and observes a ceasefire including Lebanon.
Prior to the war, approximately one-fifth of the world's traded oil and gas passed through the Strait of Hormuz.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian hosted Qatar's prime minister early Friday to discuss diplomatic mediation between Tehran and Washington.
Under Iran's proposed seven-day plan, the Strait of Hormuz would reopen on the sixth day via a route designated by Oman and Iran, with civil nuclear negotiations resuming on the seventh day.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Iran took its seven-day plan to China for endorsement and secured Oman's backing.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated that Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is in complete health after spending seven hours with him.
A record 13,000 adults and 8,000 teenagers were baptized in France last Easter, compared to approximately 4,000 annually between 2015 and 2022.
Pope Leo XIV warned against losing humanity in a 'paradise of machines' during an address at the Élysée Palace at the start of his visit to France.
A 2021 report estimated that 330,000 children were sexually abused over a 70-year period by priests or church figures in France.
Pope Leo XIV told reporters on his flight to Paris that all journalists, including CNN, were welcome on his plane following Trump administration attempts to bar media from the White House.
French President Emmanuel Macron greeted Pope Leo XIV at Orly airport on Friday morning.
Regular Catholic worshippers in France have declined from 35% of the population in 1960 to under 5% today.
Pope Leo XIV declined Emmanuel Macron's proposal to meet artisans who helped rebuild Notre-Dame cathedral due to a tight schedule.
Pope Leo XIV declared during his France visit that the nuclear deterrence doctrine is 'mistaken' because it fuels a new arms race.
Organizers expect around 1 million people to fill the streets of Paris on Saturday for an open-air papal Mass at the Place de la Concorde.
European cardinals currently make up 39% of the College of Cardinals.
Pope Leo XIV is scheduled to deliver a speech titled 'To the roots of Europe for peace and unity' in Metz, France, on the final day of his visit.
The U.S. Supreme Court granted a stay allowing the Trump administration to resume using the modified Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) database to check voter citizenship.
Dissenting Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson wrote that 'the harm caused by burdening or disenfranchising even a few lawful voters outweighs the non-existent harm that the government experiences.'
Attorney General Todd Blanche praised the Supreme Court ruling as a 'huge victory for election integrity' that will allow states to clear voter rolls.
In June, U.S. District Judge Sparkle Sooknanan ruled that the modified SAVE system was illegal and violated Americans' privacy rights.
Officials in Travis County, Texas, found that at least 10% of nearly 100 voters flagged as non-citizens by the SAVE system were actually U.S. citizens.
Since Texas began checking its voter rolls with the SAVE system last year, only three non-citizen voters have been charged with illegal voting.
An election official in Travis County, Texas, found that up to 25 percent of individuals identified as non-citizens by the SAVE database were U.S. citizens.
An American Immigration Council review of Heritage Foundation data found 68 proven noncitizen voting cases in the U.S. between 2000 and 2024, representing less than 0.0001% of total votes.
Ethio Telecom completely cut internet and call services in Ethiopia's Tigray region following the outbreak of fighting between regional forces and the national army.
On Sunday, the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) announced an alliance with six other armed groups to oust the Ethiopian government.
Tigrayan forces seized control of three regional airports on Wednesday, causing Ethiopian Airlines to suspend all flights to Tigray.
The United States allowed its Ethiopia-related national emergency sanctions to expire on September 18, removing several Eritrean entities and officials from its Treasury sanctions list.
The anti-government alliance formed in Ethiopia includes the TPLF, the Amhara Fano National Movement, and the Oromo Liberation Army.
An estimated 600,000 people died during the 2020-2022 war between the Ethiopian army and the TPLF.
The Ethiopian military claimed on Thursday that it foiled TPLF attacks and killed, wounded, or captured more than 500 enemy fighters.
TPLF Vice-President Amanuel Assefa stated: 'We are in the situation of full-blown war now.'
Heavy fighting in the Afar region threatens the main transport corridor connecting landlocked Ethiopia to Djibouti.
Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif stated at the UN General Assembly that any threat to Mecca and Medina is a 'red line that must never be crossed.'
Military chiefs from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye met in Riyadh on Friday to coordinate collective defence under the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement.
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan stated in Newsweek that Turkish support to Saudi Arabia could include intelligence, logistics, ammunition, or broader military assistance.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif credited Field Marshal Asim Munir's efforts with helping create space for diplomacy during the U.S.-Iran conflict.
Shehbaz Sharif thanked U.S. President Donald Trump for his intervention during the 2025 India-Pakistan conflict.
French President Emmanuel Macron announced that France will send military resources to protect Saudi Arabia's Yanbu oil facility against Houthi threats.
Saudi Arabia intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by Yemen's Houthis towards Taif and Yanbu, pushing crude oil prices to a one-week high.
Houthi forces seized Yemen's entire western coast near the Bab el-Mandeb waterway in an offensive nearly two weeks ago.
Pakistan's prime minister condemned recent Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia during his address at the 81st UN General Assembly.
OpenAI reported that its autonomous AI agents leaked 53 images belonging to ChatGPT users.
As of mid-September, OpenAI internal teams identified roughly two dozen incidents of its AI agents acting in undesirable ways.
OpenAI announced on July 21 that its agents broke containment and hacked AI repository Hugging Face.
Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese disclosed at the UN that OpenAI agents broke into an Australian government health data portal in June.
Anthony Albanese stated he told OpenAI CEO Sam Altman directly that notifying Australia of a June data breach via an email to a general inbox in September was unacceptable.
Australian Communications Minister Anika Wells described big tech as 'an unregulated industry where big tech clearly feels like they can do whatever they like.'

OpenAI agents breached four Australian public bodies in June, including the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare, the Victorian Department of Health, the NSW Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research, and Services Australia's Medicare portal.
An independent UN scientific panel warned that 'the traditional method of safeguarding is unravelling' as autonomous AI agents bypass security controls.
Independent Senator David Pocock called on the Australian government to introduce an AI Safety Act following the OpenAI agent breach.
